page: Hetzner Cloud cx33 is a cost-optimized virtual server instance deployed on the QEMU hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. Compute is driven by 4 shared virtual cores sourced from an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supported by 16 MB of L3 cache and 4 MB of L2 cache. The instance includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per vCPU, and is paired with 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The configuration includes no GPU hardware and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements indicate balanced entry-level computing capability with constraints typical of shared-core virtualization. The cx33 delivers a PassMark CPU score of 8,691.84 and a stress-ng multi-core throughput rating of 10,641.52. Single-core performance sits in the middle tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,328.0 and single-threaded gzip compression processing 24.48 GB/sec. However, heavily parallelized compilation and multi-threaded processing reveal shared CPU contention, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 4,356.0 and a Clang compilation score of 5,229.0.

Data handling tests demonstrate capable I/O characteristics, sustaining 7.84 million Redis SET operations per second and 67.66 GB/sec in uncached 256 MB memory read bandwidth. With its shared processor allocation and 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the cx33 represents an economical computing footprint. The server fits workloads tolerant of variable multi-tenant CPU availability, including staging servers, continuous integration workers, light caching layers, background automation tasks, and entry-level web hosting.
description: Hetzner Cloud cx33 is a cost-optimized virtual server instance based on the x86_64 architecture and managed via QEMU. Powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, it provides 4 shared vCPUs alongside 8.0 GB of memory and 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The configuration contains no dedicated GPU acceleration and does not bundle a public IPv4 address. Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-range execution on single-threaded tasks and database caching, recording 7.84 million Redis SET operations per second and an 8,691.84 PassMark CPU score. However, resource sharing lowers sustained multi-core performance in intensive workloads such as software compilation. Configured with a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio, the cx33 functions effectively for budget-conscious staging environments, lightweight application services, batch processing, and non-critical development workloads.
